transcript.content: Hello, thank you for coming in. Can you tell me what's been troubling you or what brings you here today?

Hi. Thanks for seeing me. Well, I guess what brings me in is that I just keep getting up when I'm really supposed to stay put. 

It's been happening a lot lately. Like, during client interviews—I work as a private investigator—I'll just stand up when I should be sitting across the desk from them. But it's not just at work. It happens during tutoring sessions, or even at my book club. People are definitely starting to notice that I just can't sit and listen, and it's becoming a bit of a problem.
Can you describe what goes through your mind when you feel the urge to get up? Do you feel restless or an inner need to move, even when you know you should stay seated?

Yeah, it's definitely a feeling of restlessness. It's like I just have this constant need to be doing something. 

Even on days when I don't have any field work, I can't just relax. I'll move straight from unpacking boxes to reorganizing my case files, and then I'm out running errands... it's honestly like I'm still out chasing a lead. I just have a really hard time just being off duty and staying still.
Do you find yourself getting easily distracted or having trouble focusing, even when you're trying to pay attention to something important?

Not really, no. I mean, I don't think I have much trouble focusing. When I'm working a case or looking into something important, I'm actually pretty locked in. I can pay attention just fine... it's just that my body wants to be up and moving while I'm doing it. So, no, getting distracted isn't really an issue for me.
Have you found yourself acting on impulse or doing things quickly without thinking them through, even if it might not have been the best idea?

No, I don't think so. I mean, I don't really rush into things without thinking them through. In my line of work, you kind of have to be pretty careful and calculated before you make a move, so I usually plan things out. So, no, acting on impulse isn't really something I've noticed or had a problem with. It's really just the physical need to keep moving that bothers me.
Does this restlessness and need to keep moving happen in all situations, like when you're at home alone, or is it mainly in certain places like work or social settings?

It happens pretty much everywhere, honestly. It's not just at work or when I'm out with people. Even when I'm home alone, just trying to wind down for the night, I still feel it. I'll be pacing the living room or finding some random chore to do because sitting on the couch just feels... uncomfortable. So yeah, it's pretty constant, no matter where I am.
Do you ever feel unusually tired or like you've lost your energy, even if you've been active or busy?

No, not really. I don't think I ever really lose my energy. If anything, it's kind of the opposite. I mean, even after a long day working a case, when I probably should be exhausted, I'm usually still pretty wired. So, no, feeling unusually tired or drained isn't really something I deal with. I usually just have too much energy, honestly.
Do you often find yourself fidgeting, tapping your hands or feet, or making small, repetitive movements, especially when you're trying to stay seated?

Yeah, I do. Like, when I'm stuck at the computer combing through records, my foot is pretty much always bouncing under the desk. I'll be clicking a pen, or... I just end up shifting around so much that I actually lose my place in what I'm reading. So, yes, that kind of fidgeting happens a lot when I'm trying to stay in one spot.
Do you ever experience muscle stiffness, spasms, or a feeling of tightness in your muscles, especially in your legs, even when you're not moving?

No, I haven't noticed anything like that. I don't get spasms or... or any real tightness in my muscles. Even when I'm sitting still and feeling antsy, my legs don't feel stiff or cramped. It's just that restless feeling. So, no, muscle stiffness isn't really an issue for me.
Do you ever find it difficult to relax or lie down, even when you're tired or trying to go to sleep, because of that restless feeling?

No, not really. I mean, I have a hard time sleeping sometimes because my mind is still going over a case, or I just feel too awake, but it's not because I can't physically lie down or relax. Once I'm in bed, I can stay there. It's just falling asleep that takes a while because I'm still feeling wired, not because my legs or anything are bothering me. So, no, the restless feeling doesn't keep me from lying down.
When you're trying to do something that requires you to stay still, like watching a movie or reading a report, do you still feel that strong need to get up and move around?

Not really, no. I mean, like I said before, I'll definitely fidget or bounce my leg while I'm reading a report or watching something. But I don't feel like I absolutely have to stand up and walk away. I can stay in my chair to get the job done... I just might not be perfectly still while I do it. But that strong urge to actually get up and pace around? No, I haven't really noticed that.
Do you ever feel a strong, uncomfortable urge to move your legs, especially when you're sitting or lying down?

No, not an uncomfortable urge. I mean, like I said, I definitely bounce my leg a lot when I'm sitting at my desk or going over a case, but it's not because my legs feel bad or because I have this... uncomfortable need to move them. It's just something I do without really thinking about it. And when I'm lying down, they don't bother me at all. So, no, I don't get that specific feeling you're talking about.
